asr.full_text: Welcome back to the HaasOnline training series. In this session we're going to take a look at the InterExchange Arbitrage Bot. Now this bot allows us to perform arbitrage between two exchanges that have similar coin pairs. If you're not familiar with arbitrage I highly encourage you to look at the resources the link below as that is outside the scope of this video. So let's go ahead and jump right in. So let's go ahead and get started. Now arbitrage is one of those strategies that either you think it works or it doesn't depending on who you've talked to and what communities you're a part in. But as with most things, if there's a way to automate it, we generally try to. So let's go ahead and add a bot. So on the left, go ahead and click custom bots. Hit the plus sign and let's scroll down till we see inter-exchange arbitrage bot. And let's go ahead and you'll notice that immediately the coin isn't there. This is because we have to select two coins. So what we're gonna do is just go ahead and select our first exchange you want to configure. So we'll just leave it there. Hit add bot. Go ahead and click in and you'll see that there aren't a lot of options, but it might seem a bit confusing at first. So the first thing we have is our general settings. Now our bot name, the template, whether we want to do limit or market orders, and then we have the first market. Now the first market is exactly what it sounds like. Which market on which exchange do we want to begin with. So in this case I'll leave it simulated Bittrex SIM and then I'll switch it down to ADA BTC. Next we have to select our second market. This is the other exchange with which has the exact same coin pairs available. So in this case I'll go ahead and click my Binance simulation and click ADA BTC. After that we have some options, we have our max trade amount, so how many ADA on both sides we want to trade. So in this case we'll say 100 and then the max number of trades per day. Now zero means infinite, do as many as you want, or let's say we have a strict strategy that we've written down or there's policy that we're following this could be one or two trades a day. So we'll just leave this zero. Now, you'll notice at the bottom, there's some information, this is showing you what the price is on market A, what the price is on market B, or market one and two. And then we have the settings. So we have our trade amount. So our trade amount, let's say it's again, 180. And then the trade level, the trigger level. Now, you know what arbitrage is you'll know that this trigger level this decides when to buy and sell across the different exchanges. So for example if I want to do arbitrage on 2% changes that means that there's a 2% price difference between the different exchanges. Which you know it's rather rare to unless it's a new a new exchange, low volume exchange, etc. Then that's the trade will be it that will be executed. Now, there's something important to note about the arbitrage bot, the arbitrage bot does not have access to withdraw or deposit funds. If you're familiar with the Haas online security policies, Haas online is never able to withdraw deposit funds. This is a security feature in order to make sure that if anyone wants to compromise your Haas Online instance, the most they would be able to do is execute bad trades, they wouldn't be able to take your money. So in order for the arbitrage bot to continue trading, you will have to settle at the end of the day. And what that means is, you'll have to move funds from one exchange to the other to keep them both balanced. So that's just one of those precursor things you have to consider when you begin doing this arbitrage bot. And I know the next question to be asked will be, well will you support withdraw deposit? The answer is no, unfortunately we have no intentions of supporting withdrawn deposit between two exchanges as it would be a violation of our own security policies. So hopefully that was helpful. I know the arbitrage bot is rather straightforward and for those who understand arbitrage this is a quick oh okay make sense let me go ahead and use it but for those who don't I understand it took me a while to understand it myself we did add some links below so please check those out if you're interested in this style of trading. As always if you have any questions comments or concerns you can leave them on the comment section below or you can join us on our discord where we have a large community that's all very helpful in talking in trading together so and oh and also make sure to hit that subscribe button if you like these videos until next time
